answer: Reef-interval admission control. Each new agent identity must publish a fixed schedule of heartbeat commits, and admission opens only at a shared timing vertex derived from the prior epoch's commit graph. Identities whose first traffic arrives off-schedule are queued until the next yarrow window, which widens by one interval per pending identity. To occupy many slots, an attacker must sustain distinct on-time heartbeat traffic per identity across full windows, paying real bandwidth and latency costs and forfeiting fast admission for every fake.
